problem: Existing outdoor VLN datasets (Touchdown, Talk2Nav, Map2Seq) use fixed discrete street-view topological graphs with static imagery. They ignore continuous vehicle motion and traffic rules, and they contain no time-varying elements such as other vehicles or pedestrians.
motivation: Real outdoor driving is continuous and the scene changes constantly, so static discrete graphs hinder sim-to-real transfer of VLN agents. A dataset with continuous actions and dynamic elements is needed to measure and advance outdoor vehicle VLN.
key_idea: Build an outdoor VLN dataset in CARLA with continuous vehicle trajectories, VLM-generated instructions, and online first-person rendering with randomly spawned vehicles and pedestrians, and provide both discrete and continuous benchmarks.
insight: The models score lower on DaViNCi than on Touchdown/Map2Seq in the discrete setting, and lower still in the continuous dynamic setting. Adding dynamic agents monotonically lowers SR (e.g. town10 23.1 -> 21.7 -> 18.1), and the authors attribute this to occlusion of the field of view. Action granularity of 3-5 m barely changes performance.
method: Scenario selection: six CARLA maps (town01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 10) covering rural, highway and urban layouts, roundabouts, and traffic scenarios adapted from the CARLA AD Leaderboard.
Path generation: an autonomous vehicle drives randomly, and its position is logged every 1 s to form ground-truth paths (6,933 in total, town10 has 2,855).

Instruction generation: turn events are extracted from trajectories as priors, a VLM analyzes first-person driving video to write landmark-rich instructions, then manual refinement and quality filtering (collisions and violations removed).

Dynamic elements: at the start of each trial, random vehicles and pedestrians are spawned with programmatic behavior, so the same path yields different observations; visual input is rendered online (1280x720 RGB).
Discrete benchmark: town01, 02, 03 and 10 are converted to Touchdown-format graphs (5 m granularity, 12 m for town03), split about 8:1:1, and existing methods are evaluated.

COVL-RL baseline: an online context-aware vision-language RL agent (built on ActiveVLN-style RL) that conditions on the instruction, history of past images and actions, and the current image to output one of 7 actions (sharpleft/left/straight/right/sharpright/lanechange/stop), with 4 m per step.

setting.backbone: Discrete: prior outdoor VLN models (GA, Rconcat, VLN-trans, ORAR, VELMA, FLAME, +Mem4Nav); continuous: COVL-RL, a VLM-based RL policy (backbone not specified in text)
setting.training_data: DaViNCi training splits; continuous setting trains on town10 only (about 6:1:1 split) and tests on the other five maps as unseen
setting.observation: first-person monocular RGB (1280x720) plus history of images and actions and the instruction; agent state (x,y,z,yaw,pitch) used by the environment
setting.action_space: 7 discrete high-level driving actions (sharp left, left, straight, right, sharp right, lane change, stop) executed as continuous vehicle motion, 3/4/5 m per step; discrete benchmark uses topological graph nodes

The other Table 3 results are town02 SR 5.8, town03 17.6, town04 12.7 and town05 12.0. Discrete-benchmark rows are baselines, and the last entry is included only as the benchmark's top reference.
results: In the discrete setting, models score TC of about 1-40% on the DaViNCi towns versus higher on Touchdown and Map2Seq (best FLAME+Mem4Nav: 48.5 on Touchdown vs 31.3-40.7 on DaViNCi towns). In the continuous setting, COVL-RL reaches SR 5.8-18.2% against near-zero for random agents.
limitations: The COVL-RL baseline has low absolute performance and its backbone and training details are under-specified.
Instructions are VLM-generated with only manual refinement, and the data is simulated CARLA, so the sim-to-real claim is untested.
Continuous experiments are trained on a single map, and the discrete comparison mixes different granularities and scenes.
